---
title: "Release issues"
description: "Closes issues with the release that ships their fix, not with the merge into dev."
---

An issue fixed on `dev` isn't fixed for your users until the next release.
`release-issues.yml` keeps issues open until then, and marks what is on
its way:

1. **mark** — when a pull request is merged into `dev`, the issues it closes
   (`Closes`, `Fixes` or `Resolves #n` in its description or commits; a mere
   `Refs #n` doesn't count) get the label `next-release` and one comment.
   GitHub itself ignores these keywords outside the default branch, so
   nothing closes yet.
2. **link** — in the release chain, before the `dev` → `main` pull request
   is merged: its description gets a block with `Closes #n` for every
   issue labelled `next-release` (open, or closed by hand as completed). The
   block is replaced on each run; no such issue is fine.
3. **swap** — after the merge, which closes them: those issues get
   `released` instead of `next-release`.

`link` and `swap` have to be jobs of your release chain itself: the merge
there uses `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which starts no other workflow. GitHub creates
the labels the first time they are used.
